official_owner_facts: FML4.0.41 registers a Night Config FileWatcher by default, including STARTUP. ConfigWatcher→ConfigTracker.loadConfig→ModConfig.setConfig→ModConfigSpec.acceptConfig→Reloading→MekanismConfigHelper.clearCache(false).
NeoForge21.1.200 ServerLifecycleHooks passes global CONFIGDIR and world override roots; ConfigTracker.resolveBasePath selects an existing override per file, otherwise the global file.
Missing target files initialize from defaultconfigs/<filename> where present, otherwise schema defaults.
ModConfigSpec.afterReload resets NONE caches only; WORLD and GAME values remain effective-old. ConfigSync sends raw file contents during configuration, not PLAY reload packets.
implementation: Existing manager owns claim, file watcher, callback dispatch and stale lifetime cancellation; all actual physical client/server config managers are connected, including worldgen.

Configured/pending values are separate from effective values; save and configuration snapshots preserve pending values. Explicit load retains full-load semantics; owner/world load retains GAME caches.

Actual loaded GeneralConfig owner is published through existing ChemicalConfigAccess; API-only consumers retain independent context fallback. RadiationValidation prioritizes a published owner and remote/integrated lifetimes are respected.
No new PLAY payload, data-map epoch, source-slice expansion, generic FML adapter or test class.
limits: Remote reconnect with pending WORLD values is covered by existing snapshot validation plus real integrated snapshot/save reads; no new simultaneous two-client restart matrix.
W-124 does not prove every possible config value/listener combination.
historical_probe_errors: First uncontrolled-world solar measurements had zero/absent energy before a later reading; the repaired scenario uses flat/plains/noon conditions and tests actual production. No solar algorithm was changed.
The first official probe assumed a mandatory world config path and failed because the actual file was global; this exposed and led to the product file-selection fix.
mdb reflection on an unmodifiable Map.get hit a JDK module access restriction; the probe used native quoted-key traversal and handles small inline maps.
